title: refactor(ci): split lint/test/release workflows, improve caching & release automation hygiene
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: CI runtime and flakiness have been increasing (esp. lint + test combined workflows). This PR splits lint, test, and release workflows to reduce mean CI walltime, improve cache hit rates, and make release automation safer. Changes focus on separating responsibilities, tightening cache keys, and adding a dry-run gating step for releases so release failures don't block merges.

Summary of changes: 
- Split .github/workflows into lint.yml, test.yml, and release.yml (replaces the previous monolithic ci.yml).
- Consolidated shared CI helper scripts into tools/ci/cache-utils.sh and .github/actions/common.
- Improved caching strategy: deterministic keys (repo+node-version+lockfile-hash+matrix-target) and partial restore to accelerate matrix jobs.
- Release workflow hygiene: add dry-run step that performs the full publish flow to a staging tag, signature verification, and an explicit human approval gate for GA publish.
- Bumped devDependencies in package.json (actions/toolkit and semantic-release helper) to address flaky plugin behavior.
- Updated docs: docs/ci.md with new workflow diagrams and troubleshooting steps.

Checklist: 
- [x] Split workflows and wire up triggers (push, pull_request, release).
- [x] Add deterministic cache keys and partial restore for matrix jobs.
- [x] Add release dry-run + signature verification + approval gate.
- [x] Update CI docs and runbook.
- [x] Verified green CI on redwood monorepo and a sample downstream repo.

Testing & validation: 
- Run on fork with full matrix; observed ~25% median walltime reduction for PR runs by avoiding running lint+test serially in same job and improving cache hits.
- Performed release dry-run on staging tag, validated artifact signatures and rollback behavior.
- Verified lint and test workflows are independently rerunnable and report correct annotations to PRs.

Rollout plan: 
1) Merge to main behind CI-protected branch.
2) Monitor CI queue/backlog & cache hit rates for 48h (observability dashboards updated).
3) If no regressions, promote the change to release branch templates.

Related: ENG-2345 (CI perf), ENG-2378 (release safety), existing GH issue #4821 (flaky-release-plugin).

Notes: consolidated several small TODOs into follow-up ticket ENG-2410 to instrument cold-cache job latency and an RFC for shared action library.
